post.description:
First step of the login flow. Returns `next_step` to tell the FE which screen to show.

| `next_step` | Meaning | Next call |
|---|---|---|
| `otp` | Email OTP sent | `POST /auth/otp/verify` |
| `mfa` | User has TOTP enrolled | `POST /auth/mfa/verify` |
| `mfa_setup` | MFA required but not enrolled yet | `POST /auth/mfa/enroll` |
| `session` | MFA freshness bypass — cookies already set, redirect to dashboard | — |

**Rate limiting:** 5 failed user attempts → 15-min lock; 20 failed IP attempts per 10 min → IP throttle.

Invalidate the current session.

**Requirements:** Valid `access_token` cookie.

**Effect:** Blacklists the current access JTI and its paired refresh JTI; removes the refresh JTI from the active sessions set. Clears both auth cookies.

**Returns:** Generic success

Invalidate all active sessions for the current user.

**Requirements:** Valid `access_token` cookie.

**Effect:** Sets a `logout_all` timestamp in Redis; all tokens issued before this timestamp are rejected on next request. Clears the entire active sessions set. Clears both auth cookies.

**Returns:** Generic success

**Returns:** `TOKEN_VALID` success — frontend can safely display the set-password form

post.description:
Complete account activation by setting the initial password.

**Requirements:**
- Valid, unexpired invitation token
- Password min 8 chars, at least 1 uppercase letter and 1 number
- `password` and `password_confirm` must match

**Effect:** Sets password hash, changes status to `active`, records `activated_at`, clears `invite_token_hash`.

**Returns:**
- `mfa_enrollment_required=False` — user can now log in normally
- `mfa_enrollment_required=True` + `mfa_token` — FE must redirect to `/auth/mfa/enroll` before login

Step 1 of MFA enrollment — generate TOTP secret and QR code.

Requires `mfa_token` with `purpose=setup`, obtained from:
- `POST /auth/set-password` (activation flow, when MFA is required)
- `POST /auth/otp/verify` (retroactive enforcement, when tenant enables MFA)

Returns a QR code PNG (base64) + manual entry key. Pass the refreshed
`mfa_token` to `/mfa/activate` to complete enrollment.

Step 2 of MFA enrollment — verify first TOTP code and activate MFA.

On success:
- Sets `mfa_enabled = True`
- Generates 10 single-use recovery codes (shown once — user must save them)
- Creates session and sets HTTP-only auth cookies

Conscious decision: no OTP step before enrollment. The `mfa_token` (issued after
password is set) + successful TOTP verify is a stronger proof than email OTP.

MFA verification on login — accepts TOTP code or recovery code.

`mfa_token` (purpose=verify) is obtained from `POST /auth/login` when the
user has `mfa_enabled = True`.

On recovery code use: the used code is invalidated and 10 new codes are
generated immediately. The new codes are returned in `new_recovery_codes` in
the response body — FE must show them to the user immediately.

post.summary: Verify email OTP and issue session
post.description:
Verify the email OTP code (used when `next_step=otp` from `/auth/login`).

1. Validates `token` (must not be expired)
2. Verifies the 6-digit OTP code (max 3 attempts)
3. Issues `access_token` + `refresh_token` as HTTP-only cookies

**Returns:** Full user object. Tokens delivered via HTTP-only Secure cookies.

Resend the email OTP for an in-progress login.

**Requirements:**
- `verification_token` from `/login` must still be valid
- 60-second cooldown between resend requests

**Returns:** Generic success — new OTP sent to email

Send a password reset link to the given email address.

**Security:** Always returns 200 regardless of whether the email exists — prevents user enumeration.

**Rate limiting:** 300s cooldown per email, max 3 requests/hour per email, IP throttle shared with login.

**Effect (if user exists):** Generates a JWT reset token (1h TTL), stores its SHA-256 hash, sends an email with the reset link.

**Returns:** Generic success regardless of outcome

get.summary: Validate password reset token before showing form
get.description:

**Checks:** JWT signature, expiry, and SHA-256 hash match against `password_reset_token_hash` in the database.

**Returns:** `TOKEN_VALID` success — frontend can safely display the reset-password form

post.summary: Set new password using reset token
post.description:
Complete the password reset flow by setting a new password.

**Requirements:**
- Valid, unexpired reset token (1h TTL)
- Password min 8 chars, at least 1 uppercase letter and 1 number
- `password` and `password_confirm` must match

**Non-MFA path:** Password updated immediately. All active sessions invalidated. Returns `mfa_required=false`.

**MFA path (privileged roles with MFA enabled):** Password staged in `pending_password_hash`, sessions NOT yet invalidated.
Returns `mfa_required=true, mfa_token=<5-min JWT>`. FE must call `POST /auth/password/reset/verify`.

post.summary: Verify MFA to complete password reset
post.description:
Complete MFA-gated password reset by verifying a TOTP or recovery code.

**Triggered when:** `POST /auth/password/reset` returned `mfa_required=true`.

**Code auto-detection:**
- 6-digit numeric → TOTP
- 20-char hex (`[0-9a-f]{20}`) → recovery code

**On success:**
- `pending_password_hash` promoted to `password`
- All previous sessions invalidated
- New session created immediately (no separate login needed)
- Auth cookies set in response

**Recovery code path:** Used code invalidated, 10 new codes generated and returned in `new_recovery_codes`. Show to user once.

**Rate limit on recovery codes:** 3 attempts / 24h per user → 429 `MFA_RECOVERY_RATE_LIMITED`.

post.summary: Rotate token pair using refresh token
post.description:
Exchange a valid refresh token for a new access + refresh token pair.

**Requirements:** Valid `refresh_token` HTTP-only cookie.

**Validations (in order):**
1. JWT signature + not expired
2. Token type must be `refresh`
3. Not blacklisted (`token:blacklist:{jti}`)
4. Not invalidated by `logout_all` timestamp
5. Server-side session exists (Redis Sorted Set)
6. Absolute session timeout not exceeded (`session_iat`, 8h max)
7. User exists and is active

**Effect:** Old refresh JTI blacklisted, new token pair issued with the same `session_iat` (preserves absolute timeout). New tokens delivered via HTTP-only Secure cookies.

**Returns:** Full user object. All failures return 401 `SESSION_EXPIRED`.

Verify and apply an email address change. No authentication required — called via link in email.

post.description:
Create and invite a new user. Requires `system_admin` role.

**Role constraints:**
- Platform roles (`system_admin`, `support_user`, `auditor`) — `tenant_id` must be null.
  Initiates a Four-Eyes governed action; returns `GovernedActionResponse` with `status=pending`.
  A second admin must approve before the user is created.
- Tenant roles (`front_office`, `back_office`, `leasing_company_user`) — `tenant_id` required, tenant must be active.
  Immediate execution; returns `UserResponse` with status `invited`.
- `auditor` — `access_valid_until` required.
- `leasing_company_user` — `lc_partner_id` required; must be a confirmed partner within the same
  tenant that is the leasing-company party of at least one non-terminated framework agreement.
  All other roles must omit `lc_partner_id` (or send `null`).

Suspend an active user. Requires `system_admin` role.

**Scheduling:**
- `effective_from <= now` — immediate suspension, logs `SUSPENDED` event
- `effective_from > now` — schedules Celery task, logs `SUSPENSION_SCHEDULED` event
- `effective_until` provided — schedules auto-reactivation via Celery

**Guard:** Cannot suspend the last active `system_admin`.

**Returns:** Updated `UserResponse` with status `suspended`

Reactivate a suspended user. Requires `system_admin` role.

**Requirements:** User must be in `suspended` status (deactivated users cannot be reactivated).

**Returns:** Updated `UserResponse` with status `active`

Permanently deactivate a user. Requires `system_admin` role.

**Scheduling:**
- `effective_from <= now` — immediate deactivation, logs `DEACTIVATED` event
- `effective_from > now` — schedules Celery task, logs `DEACTIVATION_SCHEDULED` event

**Guard:** Cannot deactivate the last active `system_admin`.

**Note:** Deactivation is permanent — deactivated users cannot be reactivated.

**Returns:** Updated `UserResponse` with status `deactivated`

Tenant is pre-created in `draft` status. The governed action remains pending
until a different system_admin approves it. On approval the tenant transitions

On reject/withdraw/expire the tenant is archived.

**Returns:** `GovernedActionResponse` with `status=pending`

CaseType.description:
PRD1042-1790 item 1 — the process a case runs, distinct from the object it runs on
(``CatalogEntityType``). Seven case types exist; only the two ``*_typed`` ones carry a
checklist in the November MVP. The other five run without a catalogue and nothing is built
to give them one (ticket: *out of scope*). The Financing is deliberately **not** a case type —
it has actions, not a workflow, and cannot own a catalogue.

CatalogState.title: CatalogState
CatalogState.description:
PRD1042-1894 Block 8 (AC §7) — the catalogue lifecycle: Draft → Active → Suspended.

A new catalogue starts DRAFT (never resolved by a case). Activation runs the validator and, on
success, makes it the one resolved for its case type + product. An Active catalogue can be
suspended (stops resolving for new cases; nothing deleted) and reactivated. Editing is in place on
any state — the audit trail is the history (no version flow). ARCHIVED is a reserved post-MVP
terminal (not reachable through this flow).

defines the checks. Two paper-form values fall away deliberately (vorhanden dropped; nicht
vorhanden + fehlt merge into NOT_IN_ORDER).

`NOT_REQUIRED` removes one from it. The standard set is never stored on the FA — reading the FA
alone gives only the deviation.

platform produces are `generated`. Drives the B10 compatibility rule — an upload task may reference
only a `requested` type, a generate task only a `generated` type.

FAAgreementLifecycle.title: FAAgreementLifecycle
FAAgreementLifecycle.description:
The *derived* agreement-level lifecycle. Computed from the anchor's stored status + termination
stamp + validity — never stored. `EXPIRED` is a past `valid_until` on an otherwise-active
agreement; `TERMINATED` is the terminal, agreement-level end. (CR-FA-04 versioning withdrawn.)

RefiLoanValueDateRule.title: RefiLoanValueDateRule
RefiLoanValueDateRule.description:
PRD1042-1799 CR-FA-01 (10 Aug 2026) — the Refi Loan Value Date (Valuta Refi-Darlehen) is a
*value-date rule*, not a currency. Confirmed values: ``first_of_month`` ("zum 01. des Monats",
5 of 7 leasing companies) and ``variable`` ("variabel", 1).

StateTransitionOutcome.title: StateTransitionOutcome
StateTransitionOutcome.description:
PRD1042-1894 Block 5 (AC §5) — permitted outcomes of a state_transition task. Per-task set
(Laurence-confirmed), not a value set of the type. Main process step 4 carries all four; package
redemption step 4's set is seed-only (OP-3, unnamed) and does not affect this schema.

effective_from.title: Effective From
effective_from.description: Suspension start — omitted/past for immediate on countersignature, future for scheduled

effective_from.title: Effective From
effective_from.description: Suspension start — past/now for immediate, future for scheduled

TaskApplicability.title: TaskApplicability
TaskApplicability.description:
PRD1042-1790 item 4/11 — when a task applies. ``rule`` is evaluated continuously (recorded
with the value read and the rule applied); ``person`` is resolved by a case worker as not
required / not available. Both the continuous evaluation and the person resolution are
case-runtime; this enum is the authoring-side attribute.

TaskResponsibleFunction.title: TaskResponsibleFunction
TaskResponsibleFunction.description:
PRD1042-1894 Block 4 (AC §5) — the responsible role is a set of {clerk, approver}. The clerk
prepares, the approver releases; the administrator (Bank Admin) is never offered (maintaining
catalogues is configuration, not case work).

TaskResponsibleRole.title: TaskResponsibleRole
TaskResponsibleRole.description:
Legacy single-value responsible role (US 15.x). Superseded by ``TaskResponsibleFunction``
(PRD1042-1894 Block 4). Kept for reading historical rows; new authoring uses ``responsible_roles``.

TaskType.title: TaskType
TaskType.description:
What a task *demands*, distinct from ``TaskCategory`` (a subject-area classification). The type
decides what opens for the worker and how the task closes.

PRD1042-1894 Block 3 (AC §5, Laurence 12 Aug): **SEVEN types**. ``four_eyes_sign_off`` was removed
— four eyes is a **flag on the task** (``four_eyes``) plus its exclusion set, NOT a kind of work
(eleven of the twelve four-eyes steps are a tick by a second person, one is a state transition).

TenantSupportResponse.title: TenantSupportResponse
TenantSupportResponse.description:
Read-only tenant view for Support Users with active grant.

Deliberately limited — governance actors, licence limits, legal hold,
and countersignatory details are excluded per US 29.4 security requirements.

VersionDiffResponse.title: VersionDiffResponse
VersionDiffResponse.description:
Field-level deltas between two versions, grouped by section.

Every compared field is returned, changed or not — the compare modal renders
unchanged rows too and highlights from `old_value != new_value` client-side.
